author: johnmyers
notes_extra: He wrote 3 6brs. 1:8 twist. Just touching the rifling, which is not COAL. The thread is Berger 90 BT.

author: spclark
notes_extra: 6HAGAR match rifle. 1:7.5 Krieger. Jumped nearly 0.080, which is not COAL. 300 yards.

author: MarkS
notes_extra: 10 twist 6BR. He said the load is on the hot side and to work up to it. The 87 gr hunting VLD is a different bullet.

author: gunsandgunsmithing
notes_extra: 90 Berger. Real stout in a few barrels. The thread is Berger 90gr BT for 6BR.

author: Kermit in Va.
notes_extra: He has shot it for about 20 years and said he does not load too hot. He also said to work up. He did not name the cartridge; the thread is 6BR.

author: marchx
notes_extra: 90gr bt at 100 m in a benchrest match. He did not name the cartridge; the thread is 6BR.

author: OMW57
notes_extra: He wrote over 30 grains of varget. 6BR Cooper, club benchrest matches.

author: Bill Norris
notes_extra: 90 GR. BERGER BT TAR. He wrote 2.337 COL at touch and seated at 2.342 COL with .005 jam. 1.758 and 1.763 are ogive figures, not COAL. 1-8 twist. No chronograph. He said to work up.

author: dstoenner
notes_extra: 90 target. .020 off the lands. Groups in the high 3s at 100 yards. Shilen and Criterion barrels.

author: Panzer22
notes_extra: 30.5 for the 90s in a .240 Tomahawk. The 29.0 H4895 is the 105s and 29.5 is the 95 Berger. He said the 90s like about 2950-3050, which is not a measured velocity for this charge. Starting at 29.0 for a 6BR is advice.
